heroHeadline: UniQure AMT-130 Shows Durable Huntington's Disease Slowdown at Four Years — Longest Durability Data Yet for Any Huntington's Gene Therapy
heroSubtitle: September 29, 2026: UniQure's AMT-130 gene therapy continues to slow Huntington's disease progression at the four-year follow-up mark, providing the longest durability data yet reported for a Huntington's gene therapy and reinforcing its clinical potential as the program advances. Earlier in September, the FDA accepted Intellia Therapeutics' BLA for lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) with Priority Review, targeting a March 10, 2027 PDUFA date — placing the world's first approved in vivo CRISPR therapy within reach.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, MHRA, NIH, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), ClinicalTrials.gov, and major science outlets. Clinical data reflects published peer-reviewed results only.
